description: Defaults and material libraries of PCB Thermal Lab. This is the file shipped with the program. A user file (user_defaults.json in the configuration folder, see Preferences) overrides only what it contains: a library entry with the same name replaces the shipped one, a new name is added, and the names in 'removed' are hidden; any other value replaces the shipped value. All numbers are typical values to start from, never the data of your material or fabricator: edit them in Preferences or copy this file's structure.

via_fills.name: Open
via_fills.note: Plated barrel with an empty core: only the copper plating conducts heat (192 K/W for a 0.3 mm via through 1.6 mm).

via_fills.name: Epoxy resin
via_fills.note: Non-conductive epoxy plug, the usual 'filled via' of a fabricator (IPC-4761 types V to VII, often capped with plated copper). It conducts about as little as FR-4: no thermal gain. JLCPCB: about 0.3 W/mK.

via_fills.name: Conductive paste
via_fills.note: Copper or silver loaded epoxy. JLCPCB quotes 8 W/mK; other sources 3 to 16. About +5 % on a 0.3 mm via.

via_fills.name: Copper
via_fills.note: Electroplated copper fill (plated shut): a real heat path, 3.3 times the plating of a 0.3 mm via.

metals.name: Aluminium
metals.note: Ferrotec material table: 204 W/mK, 2.71 g/cm3, 0.90 J/gK.

metals.name: Carbon steel
metals.note: Engineering ToolBox: 54 W/mK (heat capacity from a textbook).

interfaces.name: Thermal paste, good (measured 0.3 K·cm²/W)
interfaces.note: Apparent conductivity including the two contact resistances (ASTM D5470 measured totals: Arctic Silver 5 0.31 K cm2/W at 23.5 um).

interfaces.name: Paste, typical default (2 W/mK, 100 µm)
interfaces.note: A typical joint on a real heatsink.

interfaces.name: Soft gap pad (3 W/mK, 0.5 mm)
interfaces.note: Gap pads are 1 to 6 W/mK and 0.5 to 1.2 mm.

dielectrics.name: FR-4 (standard)
dielectrics.note: Glass-reinforced epoxy: 0.29 to 0.34 W/mK across, about 0.9 in the plane.

package_theta.name: QFN / exposed pad
package_theta.note: Indicative ranges from web summaries of vendor notes, NOT from a datasheet: use the datasheet value whenever there is one. θJC(top) 27 K/W is the TPS7A47 datasheet value (VQFN-20); the others are assumed typical for a plastic mould.

package_theta.name: Power QFN
package_theta.note: θJC(top) assumed (30 K/W, as in the CSD17308Q3 study).

package_theta.name: TO-220
package_theta.note: θJC(top) assumed; the metal tab is the usual heat path.

package_theta.name: SMA / SMB / SMC diode (junction to terminal)
package_theta.note: The SMA value is the SS12 datasheet junction-to-terminal figure. θJC(top) assumed (60 K/W); Tj max 125 degC is the SS12 datasheet value.

package_theta.name: Chip resistor 0603 (derived from its rating)
package_theta.note: Derived from a 0.1 W rating at 70 degC and a 170 degC limit. No top path (0 = not used); 170 degC is the limit of its derating curve.

heatsinks.name: Pin-fin 10×10, natural
heatsinks.note: Wakefield-Vette 901-10-1-18-2-B-0 (push-pin, 10 × 10 mm): 11.4 K/W in natural convection, 5.97 K/W with forced air (catalogue). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: Pin-fin 10×10, forced air
heatsinks.note: Same part with forced air (the catalogue does not state the speed here). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: Adhesive pin 10×10×12.5
heatsinks.note: Fischer Elektronik ICK 10 × 10 × 12.5 mm, adhesive or foil mounting: 26.3 K/W (archived catalogue sheet). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: TO-220 clip-on, thin
heatsinks.note: Fischer Elektronik FK 242 SA 220 O: 26 K/W (distributor listing). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: TO-220 clip-on, PF745
heatsinks.note: Aavid / Thermalloy PF745, 21.8 × 19.1 × 10 mm: 23.1 K/W (distributor listing). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: TO-220 clip-on, FK 240
heatsinks.note: Fischer Elektronik FK 240 SA 220 O: 16 K/W (distributor listing). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: TO-220 board-level, natural
heatsinks.note: Wakefield-Vette 272-AB: 10.5 K/W in natural convection, 3.6 K/W at 400 LFM (2 m/s) (DigiKey listing). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: TO-220 board-level, 2 m/s
heatsinks.note: Same part at 400 LFM (about 2 m/s). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.name: BGA 40×40×18, natural
heatsinks.note: SAME Sky HSB16-404018 (adhesive): 7.68 K/W at 75 K rise, 10.8 K/W at 1 W; 2.5 K/W at 200 LFM (about 1 m/s) and 1.5 K/W at 400 LFM (about 2 m/s). Natural convection resistance falls as the rise grows (Boyd/Aavid quote it at a 75 K rise). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.

heatsinks.note: Same part at 400 LFM (about 2 m/s). A catalogue value for its own test conditions: yours depends on the air flow, orientation and mounting.
